title: Bob Marley's birth chart
metaDescription: Bob Marley's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.6° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.1° separates Venus and Saturn from an exact square; at that range taste and structure read as one mechanism. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 17.6° Aquarius, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aquarius (2.0°), Venus in Aries (4.4°), Mars in Capricorn (24.1°): thought that travels by comparison, attraction declared rather than implied, effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Venus to Saturn, a square with 0.1° of slack. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Uranus sextile Pluto at 0.2°, and Saturn square Neptune at 1.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Venus opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, five placements stand out. The Sun in Aquarius at 17.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Aries at 4.4° is in detriment; Mars in Capricorn at 24.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Virgo at 26.5° is in detriment; Saturn in Cancer at 4.5° is in detriment. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 air, 2 fire, 2 earth, 1 water by element and 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable by modality. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.4° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
